headline: Ottawa Senators Sign Head Coach Travis Green To Multi-Year Extension
take:
The Hockey News reports that the Ottawa Senators have signed head coach Travis Green to a multi-year extension, while Daily Faceoff adds that Green has led the club to two consecutive playoff appearances, their first since 2017.

The early numbers say Ottawa's 6-3-0 start, good for 12 points in nine games, is a bit better than the underlying play. The Senators' share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality, where 50% is an even split) is 50.6% so far this season, and 49% at five-on-five, so they are roughly breaking even rather than dominating. The gap shows in goals minus expected, which sits at -3.8: the skaters have scored well below what their chances suggest. Goalies have covered for that, with goals saved above expected at +2.2, meaning the netminding has stopped more than the shot quality predicted. The special teams look steady, not elite: the power play generates 0.82 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allows 0.75. For Green, the extension rewards results, but the data suggests the finishing should improve, and that matters more than the record if the goaltending cools.
